data.title: Choose the right Power BI MCP server
data.summary: Query a report, change a semantic model, or support an older client: start with the right connection.

facts.text: Microsoft recommends Fabric IQ for consumption. It is generally available and reads reports and semantic models using delegated user access; RLS and OLS apply.
Fabric IQ uses Streamable HTTP at https://fabriciq.svc.cloud.microsoft/v1/mcp/fabriciq. Its client discovers tools at runtime; service-principal authentication is unsupported.

The earlier Consumption endpoint remains preview at https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/powerbi. It requires tenant enablement and Build permission. Its Generate Query tool additionally requires Copilot licensing; client-generated DAX is an alternative.

Authoring changes semantic models. Hosted is preview at https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/powerbi/authoring; local is GA and also reaches Desktop, PBIP and TMDL files. This is separate from report-building skills.

A Microsoft Entra work or school account with access to the target content; check the selected server’s own requirements.

Use the older Consumption endpoint only when that is the integration you intend to support.

Read the intended model’s schema and reconcile one known total before broader analysis.
limitations: Sintra documents these servers; it does not connect to your tenant.

data.title: Explain budget variance with Power BI
data.summary: A complete synthetic example: sample data, read-only DAX, a reconciled revenue bridge and evidence an LLM can retrieve.

facts.text: Fabric IQ exposes discovery, metadata and DAX execution tools. The calling agent composes the analysis; the server does not supply a natural-language answer itself.
DAX DIVIDE returns BLANK for a zero denominator by default. SUMMARIZECOLUMNS groups query results; this example uses query-scoped measures and explicit entity, period and currency filters.

sources.title: Fabric IQ MCP: setup and tool contract
DIVIDE function
SUMMARIZECOLUMNS function

prerequisites: Access to the finance report through Fabric IQ.
Actual and budget measures, fiscal period, reporting currency, sign convention and entity scope agreed with the report owner.
steps: Find the finance report and inspect its filters, schema and measure definitions.
Resolve the exact entity and period values. Reuse the approved measures in a read-only DAX query.
Compare actual and budget at the same grain. Separate absolute variance from percentage variance; flag a zero budget.
Reconcile the total to the report. Attribute drivers only where returned data supports them; list unexplained residuals.
data.output: Variance table, query and filter receipt, driver commentary, and open questions.
validation: The query total matches the report under identical filters.
Driver amounts sum to total variance; currency, period and denominator are explicit.
Narrative distinguishes observed differences from causal hypotheses.
limitations: The public synthetic calculation is tested and cross-checked against HoldingCo. Power BI DAX, Power Query, OAuth, MCP, permissions and live tenant totals have not been exercised.
Commentary is authored from deterministic results; no LLM quality benchmark or business impact is claimed.
This revenue-only example rejects negative inputs and missing scenario rows. Expense favorability, credits, FX and real fiscal calendars need separate policies.
An LLM explanation cannot establish causality from aggregated variance alone.
data.prompt: Using my accessible finance report, inspect the schema and report filters first. For [entity], [fiscal period] and [currency], compare the approved Actual and Budget measures at the same grain. Show DAX, filters, absolute variance and percentage variance, handling a zero budget explicitly. Reconcile to the report total, then describe supported drivers and unexplained residuals. Do not modify the model or invent figures.

data.title: Review a DAX measure change before applying it
data.summary: Use Authoring MCP to inspect a model, propose a small change and compare results against a baseline.

A definition of the requested metric, expected totals and review owner.
steps: Identify the model and inspect existing measures and dependencies before creating anything.
Capture baseline DAX and results for normal, blank, zero-denominator and subtotal cases.
Propose the smallest change and show its diff. Apply it to the development copy after review.
Run the same queries and record differences. Keep the reviewed model change in source control.
data.output: A reviewable measure diff with before/after query results.
validation: Expected totals and subtotals pass the agreed cases.
No duplicate measure or unintended relationship change is introduced.
limitations: Example procedure; no Power BI model was modified or tested by Sintra.
Semantic model authoring does not by itself mean a finished report or visual was created.

Capture baseline results and test normal, blank, zero-denominator and subtotal cases. Present the change for review before applying it. Return before/after results and any unresolved assumptions.

data.title: Audit an existing Excel model with Claude
data.summary: Trace formulas, review suspicious assumptions and produce a cell-linked exception log before changing the workbook.

facts.text: Claude for Excel supports workbook questions with cell citations, error tracing and model edits. It is available on eligible paid Claude plans; supported Excel builds and organization settings apply.

Crunched: Excel modeling for investors and advisors

Open each cited cell and compare its formula and input lineage yourself. Distinguish an error from a legitimate policy choice.

Save the reviewed version and exception log, keeping unresolved issues visible.

data.title: Build a checked analysis inside Excel with Copilot
data.summary: Plan the analysis, create workbook-native formulas and reconcile results against the existing public variance example.

facts.text: Copilot in Excel offers edit, plan and chat modes on supported Windows, Mac and web clients. Edit mode changes the workbook; chat can analyze without editing. Availability depends on the account and client.

sources.title: Get started with Copilot in Excel

data.title: Create a cited decision brief with Microsoft 365 Researcher
data.summary: Combine authorized work context and primary web sources into a reviewable brief with contradictions and open questions.

facts.text: Researcher is found under Agents in Microsoft Copilot and produces structured, cited research from web sources and accessible work content. Its current guide lists eligible personal and commercial subscriptions; Claude model access additionally needs administrator enablement.

sources.title: Get started with Researcher in Microsoft Copilot

Separate established facts, competing interpretations and unanswered questions. Remove unsupported recommendations.
Save the reviewed brief and source inventory for the next research cycle or presentation.

validation: Material claims are supported by the cited page or document, not just a search snippet.
The brief respects the requested time window and makes contradictory evidence visible.

Claude in Researcher is a tenant-controlled option; do not assume availability from a separate Claude subscription.

data.title: Build a source-grounded PowerPoint slide with Copilot
data.summary: Turn a specific section of an approved file into a slide, then verify its facts, layout and fit with the existing deck.

facts.text: PowerPoint's documented add-a-slide flow lets you reference a file from the Copilot interface. The separate presentation-creation guide currently says file referencing is coming soon to Agent Mode; these are different routes.

sources.title: Add a slide from a file with Copilot in PowerPoint
Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint

prerequisites: An eligible Copilot-enabled PowerPoint client and access to the intended source file.
The existing deck/template, the relevant source section and an agreed audience.
steps: Open a review copy of the existing deck. Identify where the new or revised slide belongs.
Open Copilot from the slide interface and request a slide grounded in a specific source section.
Use Reference a file or the slash file picker in the documented add-slide flow; choose the exact authorized file/version.
Ask for one decision-focused slide using the deck's existing visual style and approved figures.
Check each material claim against the source, then inspect chart labels, notes, reading order and text fit.
Save the reviewed slide/deck with the source reference. If only topic-based Agent Mode is available, record the limitation rather than claiming file grounding.
data.output: A reviewed source-grounded slide in the existing presentation, with a traceable source reference.
validation: The slide is grounded in the selected file and section; unsupported content is removed or flagged.
Layout, units, chart labels and speaker notes survive slideshow/export review.
limitations: Source-backed recipe; no PowerPoint session was executed by Sintra.
UI routes and rollout differ. A topic-generated deck is not evidence that the selected file was read.

data.title: Turn a Teams meeting into a checked action register
data.summary: Separate decisions, commitments and open questions, then export a reviewed action table to Excel where policy allows.

facts.text: Copilot can use a meeting's transcript and chat for follow-up. Post-meeting questions require an available transcript. Table responses can be opened in Excel, subject to meeting export and sensitivity settings.

sources.title: Catch up on meetings with Microsoft Copilot in Teams

prerequisites: An eligible Copilot account and access to the intended Teams meeting.
An existing transcript and permission to use/export the meeting content; avoid changing recording policy for this exercise.
steps: Open the exact meeting chat or Recap and confirm its date, participants and transcript availability.
Ask Copilot for separate decisions, assigned actions and open questions, citing transcript/chat evidence.
Request an action table with owner, commitment, due date, source and status. Keep unstated owners/dates unassigned.
Check every commitment against the cited passage. A suggestion is not an accepted task.
Where policy permits, use Open in Excel for the table and compare the exported rows to the reviewed register.
Resolve ambiguous commitments with the responsible people through your normal process before assigning or syncing tasks.
data.output: A reviewed action register with source references, unresolved owners/dates and a clear meeting identity.
validation: Actions and dates match what was actually agreed; no owner or deadline is fabricated.
Exported rows match the reviewed table and respect the meeting's restrictions.
limitations: Recipe not executed in Teams by Sintra. No messages, Planner tasks or notifications are created by this guide.
No transcript means no substantiated post-meeting spoken-content analysis; export can be disabled by policy.
data.prompt: From this meeting's accessible transcript and chat, separate decisions, agreed actions and open questions. Return an action table with owner, commitment, due date, evidence passage and confidence. Leave unstated owners and dates unassigned. Distinguish proposals from accepted commitments. Prepare an Excel-ready register but do not create tasks or send follow-ups.
